content.title: Michigan vs UConn score, highlights in March Madness national title game
content.text: April 6, 2026Updated April 7, 2026, 12:36 a.m. ETIt wasn't the prettiest game for Michigan basketball, but a national title is coming to Ann Arbor, nonetheless.Completing arguably the most successful season in program history, the 1-seed Wolverines beat the 2-seed UConn Huskies 69-63 in the national final of the 2026 NCAA Tournament on Monday, April 6, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The win gives the Wolverines their second national championship in men's basketball, with the banner from their 1989 title now awaiting its companion at Crisler Center.Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau was the team's best player in the final, finishing the game with 19 points in a game where the Michigan offense failed to establish consistency for the entire first half and much of the second. For his efforts, he was named the Final Four Most Outstanding Player.Big man Yaxel Lendeborg, who played with injuries to his left knee and ankle suffered during the national semifinal win against Arizona, initially struggled on offense but ended up scoring 13 points while playing in a team-high 36 minutes.Buy Michigan championship books, newspapersBut even though Michigan's offense wasn't as explosive as it had been it its five previous tournament games, the Wolverines defense kept UConn at bay, recording six steals and six blocks while switching effectively to counter the Huskies' aggressive ball movement. Michigan also kept UConn ineffective from distance later in the game, with the Huskies at one point missing 12 straight 3-pointers from the end of the first half into the second half.Perhaps Michigan's key to victory, however, was its free-throw shooting. The Wolverines drew fouls early and took advantage of the charity stripe, shooting 25-for-28 from the free-throw line and giving themselves scoring opportunities when their field goal attempts weren't falling.And doing as they've done all year, the Wolverines found a different way to win, with nothing left to prove in a championship-winning season.Here's how it all went down. Yaxel Lendeborg cuts down the netsLendeborg will be preparing for the NBA draft soon, but for now he gets to enjoy his national championship celebration. Elliot Cadeau named Most Outstanding PlayerMichigan point guard Elliot Cadeau was named the 2026 Final Four Most Outstanding Player, and it was well-deserved.Cadeau led all scorers with 19 points in the final against UConn, leading a struggling offense while finding creative ways to put points on the board. He averaged 16 points, six assists and three steals per game over Michigan's two Final Four wins. Dusty May: 'It still doesn't feel real'In his postgame interview with TBS's Ernie Johnson, Michigan coach Dusty May said, "It still doesn't feel real. It feels like we still have another game to prepare for."Here is his interview with Tracy Wolfson. Yaxel Lendeborg: 'We're the best team in college basketball'Michigan star Yaxel Lendeborg is now a college champion, making his case for Michigan basketball's march to the title. Michigan beats UConn, wins national titleFINAL: Michigan 69, UConn 63.Michigan freshman Trey McKenney hit both his free throws with 13 seconds left, giving Michigan the cushion they needed to seal a national title.This is Michigan's second-ever national title in men's basketball. UConn misses 3-pointer, Michigan rebounds with 13 seconds left2H, 0:13: Michigan 67, UConn 63.Michigan guard Roddy Gayle missed both free throws with 30 seconds left, but guard Trey McKenney grabbed a key rebound following an Alex Karaban miss on a 3-point attempt. One made free throw should seal this for the Wolverines. Solo Ball makes key 3-pointer to keep UConn alive2H, 0:37: Michigan 67, UConn 63.A Solo Ball three-pointer off the bank shot keeps UConn in the game. Michigan is sweating now. Michigan less than a minute from a title2H, 0:48: Michigan 67, UConn 60.UConn is chipping away at the lead, but Michigan is firmly in the drivers' seat. If the Wolverines hold onto the ball and make their free throws, a title will be theirs. Trey McKenney hits key 3-pointer to stop UConn's momentum2H, 1:49: Michigan 65, UConn 56.Former Michigan center Tarris Reed Jr. made two free throws for the Huskies to cut Michigan's lead to seven points once again. The points gave Reed 11 points, giving him a double-double along with his 13 rebounds.UConn then cut the Michigan lead to six points on a long 3-pointer from forward Alex Karaban, but a Trey McKenny 3-pointer two possessions later erased UConn's momentum. Michigan has a 9-point lead with less than two minutes to play. Yaxel Lendeborg in double figures2H, 3:48: Michigan 60, UConn 51.Lendeborg followed his own miss with a tip-in layup to put himself into double-digit scoring for the game. That was followed by a Braylon Mullins 3-pointer, his second in a row, cutting the Michigan lead to seven points.Lendeborg then drew a shooting foul and made both his free throws, bringing him to 13 points on the game. He is one of three Wolverines in double figures, with point guard Elliot Cadeau (15) and big man Morez Johnson Jr. (12) joining him. UConn makes first 3-pointer of second half2H, 5:21: Michigan 56, UConn 48.UConn shooter Braylon Mullins made a 3-pointer just before the half, ending a streak of 12-straight missed 3-pointers for the Huskies. But Michigan had already built a double-digit lead by then, with a layup from Lendeborg (assisted by Elliot Cadeau) helping Michigan set the pace.UConn is capable of a comeback, but with how slow their offensive sets develop, the Huskies are running low on time. Michigan hanging onto lead in scrappy second half2H, 7:16: Michigan 52, UConn 45.UConn's shots are not falling, as the Huskies are 0-for-9 from beyond the 3-point line so far in the second half. But they have found enough inside scoring to hang around with Michigan, even though the Wolverines have already blocked six UConn shots so far.Scrappy efforts from big men Morez Johnson and Aday Mara have led to key buckets, allowing Michigan to keep its distance. But this is far from the prettiest game, and it's not clear if Michigan can hold onto its lead while playing UConn's brand of basketball. Especially when Lendeborg, the team's leading scorer this season, is only 2-for-10 shooting from the floor and 0-for-5 from 3. Elliot Cadeau makes back-to-back buckets2H, 12:47: Michigan 48, UConn 37.An impressive isolation take from Michigan freshman Trey McKenney with the shot clock winding down gave the Wolverines a 43-35 lead, their largest of the game so far. Point guard Elliot Cadeau followed that with a layup and followed that with a heat-check 3-pointer in the next possession, giving him a game-high 15 points.Michigan now leads by double digits after Cadeau's 3-pointer, Michigan's first of the night. Michigan extends lead in second half2H, 15:16: Michigan 40, UConn 33.It's been a defensive battle so far in the second half, with an Aday Mara full-court pass to Nimari Burnett leading to two made free throws and the first points of the half.Otherwise, sloppy play has defined the first few minutes of the second half, with UConn turning the ball over four times and Michigan three. Michigan holds onto a lead but hasn't yet found any consistency on offense, though it has found some success with drawing fouls on penetration attempts. Yaxel Lendeborg: 'I feel awful'Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg was interviewed by TBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson and gave a surprisingly candid response to her question about his condition."I feel awful, I feel super week right now," he said, adding that he's not making his shots and that he's playing soft. Lendeborg has four points on 1-for-5 shooting so far in the first half, shooting 2-for-2 from the free-throw line while playing all 20 minutes of the half."I missed the plays I don't usually miss, I had many opportunities to take advantage of a smaller defender, haven't been able to do it," he said. "I played really soft in that first half and I'm gonna do way better in the second half."Lendeborg and UConn forward Alex Karaban are the only two players who played all 20 minutes of the first half. Lendeborg also has two personal fouls, no rebounds, no assists and no turnovers. Michigan leads at the halfEnd 1H: Michigan 33, UConn 29.Michigan center Aday Mara has made his last three shots after missing his first three early in the half. His post play has given the Wolverines another dimension in a challenging offensive half for Michigan.A Roddy Gayle Jr. putback dunk but an exclamation point on the half for Michigan. The Wolverines will likely need to play a lot better on offense in the second half to lock up a title, but the Michigan defense is holding up quite well so far. Michigan on 6-0 run1H, 2:24: Michigan 29, UConn 25.A hook-and-hold foul on UConn forward Alex Karaban gave the Wolverines free throws and possession, and a Yaxel Lendeborg layup gave the Wolverines a 27-25 lead with under three minutes left. Center Aday Mara followed with an inside basket, extending a 6-0 run for the Wolverines. Michigan and UConn trading leads1H, 3:58: UConn 25, Michigan 23.Two made free throws from Michigan guard Nimari Burnett retook the lead for the Wolverines with under seven minutes left. The preceding foul was UConn's seventh, meaning the Wolverines will be shooting 1-and-1s for the rest of the half.Meanwhile, Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau picked up his second foul and went to the bench, likely for the rest of the half, with Roddy Gayle Jr. replacing him on the floor. And while Cadeau isn't the team's leading scorer (Morez Johnson with eight points), he's been arguably the most important player on the floor.Some good news for the Wolverines: Lendeborg knocked down both of his free throws to give Michigan a 21-20 lead and his first points of the game, though UConn freshman Braylon Mullins knocked down a 3-pointer to retake the lead for the Huskies.Neither team is shooting well, with UConn 9-for-24 and Michigan 7-for-22 on the floor, but the Huskies are benefitting from long possessions and second-chance baskets off offensive rebounds. But on the bright side for Michigan, the Wolverines are 9-for-10 from the free-throw line while the Huskies have made only three free throws. UConn takes first lead1H, 7:00: UConn 18, Michigan 17.An Alex Karaban corner 3-pointer gave UConn its first lead of the game at 16-13 midway through the first half. Michigan is struggling on offense early on, shooting just 7-for-19 from the floor while having yet to make a 3-pointer.Lendeborg has zero points on only two shot attempts, but big man Morez Johnson Jr. has picked up the slack with eight points on 4-for-5 shooting. Maybe even more worrying is center Aday Mara, who led the Wolverines with 26 points in the national semifinal against Arizona, with only two points so far this game (though he has provided his typically excellent interior defense). Yaxel Lendeborg injury updateYaxel Lendeborg emerged from the locker room with tape around his left knee, but no brace. He jumped, shuffled laterally and participated in full activities with Michigan as the team warms up.After shooting around, the first team All-American ended his warmup routine with his signature bounce-pass self alleyoop with teammate Roddy Gayle Jr. He didn't appear to have his usual explosion, but was able to get up for the slam.He's listed in the starting lineup and will give it a go in the national championship.-Tony Garcia, Detroit Free Press UConn hanging around1H, 11:57: Michigan 11, UConn 10.A Solo Ball 3-pointer cut Michigan's lead to two points, but Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau responded with a tough reverse layup while drawing a foul (he missed the subsequent free throw). He leads all players with seven points.Michigan's defense has been especially aggressive, causing a shot-clock violation and almost causing a 10-second backcourt violation on UConn. But the Huskies have been up to the challenge, taking their time with their halfcourt offense and knocking down key 3-pointers to keep pace with the Wolverines. Michigan takes early lead1H, 15:41: Michigan 9, UConn 4.Michigan missed its first two shots of the game before big man Morez Johnson Jr. took advantage of a mismatch and put up a layup to make the game 2-0 Michigan. Point guard Elliot Cadeau later drew a shooting foul beyond the three-point line and made all three free throws to give Michigan a 7-2 lead.Big man Yaxel Lendeborg doesn't have a shot attempt so far, but seems to be moving a lot better than he did in the second half of the Arizona game. Yaxel Lendeborg startingMichigan has released its starting five, with Yaxel Lendeborg listed as a starter. Lendeborg hurt his knee and his ankle in the Wolverines' 91-73 win over Arizona in the national semifinal on Saturday, but looks ready to go for tonight's game against the Huskies. UConn starting fiveUConn has released its starting lineup, with injured guard Solo Ball listed among the starting five. Michigan at shootaroundMichigan is warming up on the floor with about a half hour left until tipoff. Yaxel Lendeborg warming upMichigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg was seen warming up before the game with only a small wrap on his injured left knee. Wolverines in the houseMichigan players have arrived to Lucas Oil Arena for the national championship game, with some arriving on foot and others on golf carts. Solo Ball injury statusPer TNT sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson, UConn guard Soloman Ball is expected to play tonight against Michigan as he is dealing with a left foot sprain suffered in UConn's Final Four win against Illinois on Saturday. Yaxel Lendeborg injury statusMichigan forward Yaxel Lendeborg is expected to start tonight after suffering an MCL sprain on his left knee during the Wolverines' 91-73 win over Arizona on Saturday.Lendeborg missed much of the second half against Arizona following the injury, but a post-game MRI came back clean. It is unclear how much the injury is currently affecting his movement. Michigan injury reportNo surprises with the pregame availability report, with Michigan listing two players as out for the national championship game.Michigan: G L.J. Cason (out), F Winters Grady (out).UConn: None listed. Where to watch the game in Metro DetroitAre you looking for the perfect sports bar to watch tonight's game?
